reference: English Vocabulary Profile A1 (family words); Cambridge A1 Movers/KET-style gap-fill
matching: Each form: items 1-2 kinship gap-fill from a definition (parent's sibling / sibling's child style), 3-4 choice between gender pairs; EC = Arabic-L1 vowel spelling slip on a kin word in a natural sentence; FP = name a named family member in one sentence; transfer = read a short family tree description and name the relation. All words EVP A1, prompts 8-14 words. Item order identical across forms: 1-2 controlled gap-fill, 3-4 controlled choice, 5-6 error correction, 7-8 free production (target_form_0_1_2), 9 transfer. Review round 1: slots 5-6 now contain a wrong kin word that must be replaced (uncle/aunt/cousin/grandmother/grandfather, all A1); C-4 now aunt. Review round 3: all items 7-8 use the 'VOCABULARY variant, named word' rubric (as C-7 already did), since each prompt names the kin word. Review round 4: the kin-word swaps (my mother's mother is my aunt ...) were factual absurdities, not learner errors. Slots 5-6 are now vowel slips on an A1 kin word: doughter/hasband (A), parints/brather (B), grandmather/nece (C). outcomes.json l1ErrorTypes = [spelling_vowel].
